title: Shivchat
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Bava Kamma 91b: “Rabbi Chanina said: My son Shivchat died only because he cut down a fig tree before its time.” Dikdukei Soferim reads “Shikhchat my son.”

In Bava Batra 26a Rashi explains: Shivchat my son — so was his name. There, at 126b: a certain man came before Rabbi Chanina and said to him, “I have a presumption about this one (whom he came to testify about) that he is a firstborn.” He said to him, “How do you know?” He said: “When people came to his father, he would say to them, ‘Go to Shivchat my son, who is a firstborn, and whose spittle heals.’” The Rashbam explains “Shivchat Beri” as the firstborn’s name, and this is not the son of Rabbi Chanina mentioned in Bava Batra 26.
Seder HaDorot already discussed at length whether his name was “Shivchat Beri” or whether his name was Shivchat; see there.

notes.text: Saved Vilna Rashbam Bava Batra126b comments on שכחת ברי as the firstborn’s name and distinguishes him from Rabbi Chanina’s son; its preceding gloss calls him שכחת. Hyman’s Shivchat form and the competing question whether Beri belongs to the name are both preserved.

The consulted Bava Batra 126b has Shikhchat beri; the Vilna Rashbam gloss calls it the firstborn’s name and explicitly distinguishes this figure from Rabbi Chanina’s son in the fig-tree account. Hyman’s Shivchat spelling and the alternative between a personal name including Beri and “my son” remain distinct. Exact Dikdukei Soferim and Seder HaDorot editions were not inspected here.
